name: Deepwell Draw — The Floating Card Game
description: A gambling card game played in bars and dens throughout Tier 1-2 districts using smart-ink cards that shift their face values at randomized intervals governed by a central house algorithm — meaning the card you hold at the start of a round may not be the card you hold when it's time to reveal. The shifting is subtle and requires players to develop a feel for the rhythm of the ink rather than memorizing fixed hands, creating a skill layer that rewards long-term players while appearing purely random to newcomers. The game takes its name from the Deepwell Den, a floating barge gambling establishment where it was first played.
story_hooks: A player wins an impossible hand — the cards shifted in a sequence that shouldn't be statistically achievable — and the house wants to know if they cracked the algorithm or if the algorithm cracked itself.
A runner is tasked with delivering a specific smart-ink deck to a specific table at a specific time — no explanation given, significant Quanta offered.
A Tier 4 corporate analyst has been slumming in Shelf dens and has reverse-engineered the ink shift pattern — they want to sell the algorithm, but to whom is the question.
